option_relations.rationale: The presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies and elevated serum IFN-β levels, along with the clinical presentation, suggests a specific subtype of juvenile dermatomyositis.
The clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not support polymorphous light eruption as the primary diagnosis.
Juvenile dermatomyositis is a broader category that encompasses the specific subtype suggested by the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies.
The clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not support systemic lupus erythematosus as the primary diagnosis.
